author: WP05
summary: Partly synchronised chapter on SpriteBatch, SpriteSortMode, SpriteEffects and SpriteFont with selected defects. Much of it is contradicted at TARGET: the rasterizer argument is honoured, states are applied at End for deferred modes, positions and glyphs stay fractional in the shared layer, sorting reproduces XNA's unstable quicksort, SpriteEffects is a flags enum, the SpriteFont reader exists and misuse throws InvalidOperationException. The site had overload lists and a sort-mode tutorial; three new deep dives and a SpriteBatch guide expansion now carry the state, sorting, batching and text-layout semantics.

concepts.text: Every public renderer identity exposes the SpriteBatch contract (2D drawing is what all 25 are built to do), but behaviour and evidence vary by implementation family.
SpriteBatch flow: Begin resolves states, Draw appends quad items, flush at End or per Draw in Immediate, optional sort, renderer grouping; one renderer submission is not one GPU draw.
concepts.note: Flush on capacity or texture change is renderer-side, not in the shared class; the figure caption says so.

concepts.text: The subject spans the SpriteBatch API, SpriteSortMode, SpriteEffects and SpriteFont plus selected defects that clarify the contract.
SpriteBatch inherits GraphicsResource and offers eight Begin overloads (the five-, six- and seven-parameter forms each with a BlendState value and a const BlendState* twin), not five.
Begin() defaults: Deferred, AlphaBlend, LinearClamp, DepthStencilState::None, CullCounterClockwise, identity transform.
Longer overloads: nullptr states fall back to the same defaults, nullptr effect to the built-in sprite shader, and the transform matrix applies to every sprite before the projection.
Source note: Begin ignored its RasterizerState parameter (commented out), unlike FNA PrepRenderState.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the resolved rasterizer state is stored and applied; the shared scissor scene is registered for SDL_GPU, SOFTWARE, VULKAN, WEBGPU and D3D11/12.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/SpriteBatch.cpp (Begin stores rasterizerState_, applyRenderState sets it); modules/graphics/examples/spritebatch_begin_rasterizerstate_scissor_test.cpp; SpriteBatchTests DeferredBeginAppliesRenderStatesOnlyWhenEndFlushes

concepts.text: Timing of state application: Deferred and sorted modes apply blend, sampler, depth-stencil and rasteriser state in End immediately before the flush; Immediate applies them in Begin (Bible: Begin applies blend and depth-stencil).
Passing a ScissorTestEnable rasteriser state to Begin now clips the batch; the device-level workaround is no longer required and a later default Begin restores CullCounterClockwise.
Draw has ten overloads: seven XNA forms and three CNAEXT conveniences (not six plus three).
XNA nullable Rectangle? source rectangles are std::optional<Rectangle>; std::nullopt means the whole texture.
DrawString has six overloads: std::string or StringBuilder, each as a four-argument form and nine-argument uniform and Vector2-scale forms.
The CNAEXT conveniences are Draw(tex, float x, float y) and two destination-rectangle forms with a plain non-optional source rectangle (the Bible counted two float forms).
Every XNA overload takes a colour tint; only CNAEXT Draw(tex, x, y) omits it (white).
tokens: the only form without a colour argument

concepts.text: The two fully parameterised position overloads differ only in whether scale is a float or a Vector2; destination size is source size times scale.
tokens: differ only in that parameter's type

concepts.text: The full destination-rectangle overload has no scale parameter because the rectangle implies it.
origin is a point in source-texel space: both the rotation pivot and the point that lands on position.
Rotating a sprite about its centre requires passing the texture (source) centre as origin.
Passing Vector2::Zero as origin pivots around the top-left corner so the sprite orbits the position, a symptom easily misdiagnosed as a rotation-math bug.

concepts.section: Vector positions are quantized before they reach a renderer
concepts.text: Claim that Vector2-position draws are stored as an integer Rectangle and truncated in the shared layer: at TARGET SpriteInfo keeps float destX/destY/destWidth/destHeight and the shared layer passes fractions through.

concepts.section: Vector positions are quantized before they reach a renderer
concepts.text: Quantisation now happens only at the renderer seam: the default float Draw truncates toward zero, and only EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE override it, so (10.9, 4.9) still becomes (10, 4) on other families.

target.evidence: IGraphicsRenderer.hpp (ISpriteBatchRenderer float Draw default); renderer overrides in easygl, opengl4, software

concepts.section: The D3D9 half-pixel offset and a mutation-testing trap
concepts.text: Direct3D 9 places texel centres at integer pixel coordinates; XNA 4.0 compensated inside the sprite projection.

concepts.section: The D3D9 half-pixel offset and a mutation-testing trap
concepts.text: Shared SpriteBatch.cpp carries no half-pixel compensation, which is correct for renderers with pixel-centre conventions.

concepts.section: The D3D9 half-pixel offset and a mutation-testing trap
concepts.text: The D3D9 compensation lives only in D3D9SpriteBatchRenderer::BuildMatrixTransformEXT, folded into the sprite projection (M41/M42 shifted by -0.5 of M11/M22).

concepts.section: The D3D9 half-pixel offset and a mutation-testing trap
concepts.text: The projection uses far plane -1, not 1: with 1 any layerDepth above 0 maps to negative D3D9 clip depth and the sprite is silently clipped.
concepts.note: The Bible snippet used far plane 1.

SpriteSortMode has five values; only BackToFront and FrontToBack order by layerDepth.
Claim that Texture mode is a stable sort on raw texture pointers: at TARGET it reproduces XNA's unstable Array.Sort quicksort on the renderer object address, descending.
The Texture-mode test establishes grouping but not preserved order: TextureGroupsDrawsAndMatchesXnaEqualKeyOrdering records the reversal of equal-key entries.
Order between texture groups is address-dependent; Texture mode is for sprites that do not overlap.
Mock renderers establish grouping but cannot observe renderer-side texture binding; pixel scenes are needed for that.

concepts.text: Claim that SpriteEffects is a plain enum class without bitwise operators: at TARGET |, &, |= and &= are defined, so FlipHorizontally | FlipVertically (3) is valid.
Claim that DrawString direction tables have three entries: they have four, masked by effects & 0x03 as in FNA.
CNA docs/spritefont-support.md still records combined flip as an open gap; the header and tests supersede it.
Earlier DrawString flipped glyph texture coordinates without mirroring the glyph sequence; FNA-shaped axis terms in shared SpriteBatch.cpp fixed every renderer at once.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the measure-first shift and per-glyph mirrored offsets are in the shared loop; the page labels the defect historical.

concepts.text: With any flip, DrawString measures the whole string first and shifts the origin on the mirrored axis so the sequence mirrors around the text block.
The BlendState from Begin (AlphaBlend by default) remains on GraphicsDevice after End, as in FNA; at TARGET so do the DepthStencilState, RasterizerState and SamplerStates[0].
concepts.note: Broadened from blend state to all four.

concepts.text: EasyGL once installed hard-coded source-alpha factors; the EasyGL_SpriteBatch_BlendStateLeak regression (grey clear, small additive sprite, opaque quad) discriminates through the green channel.

EasyGL limitation: a full-back-buffer SpriteBatch draw before the frame's first 3D draw was reported to break that frame; not root-caused; the blend regression avoids it with a 4 x 4 sprite. A later neutral scene did not reproduce it on EasyGL or Vulkan.
concepts.note: Issue candidate WP05-i016; stated on the page as unresolved in CNA records.

concepts.text: SpriteFont is not a GraphicsResource; it owns the atlas by value plus glyph bounds, cropping, characters, line spacing, spacing, kerning and an optional default character.
Claim that CNA lacks the XNB SpriteFont reader: SpriteFontContentTypeReader exists; the CNAEXT public constructor remains for tools and tests.
MeasureString exists for String and StringBuilder; the StringBuilder overload forwards because C++ has no garbage-collection reason to duplicate it.
A trailing newline adds a second empty line: height 2 x LineSpacing when no glyph is taller, matching XNA.
CNA String is UTF-8 std::string; SpriteFont and SpriteBatch decode each code point with DecodeUtf8CodePoint.
Glyph keys are 16-bit charcs, so only Basic Multilingual Plane characters can be glyphs; a well-formed code point above U+FFFF decodes to ?.
Invalid or truncated UTF-8 decodes to ? and advances at least one byte; the ? is then looked up like any character (default character or ArgumentException).
tokens: advances by at least one byte

concepts.text: SpriteFont surface, MeasureString, glyph placement, newline, default character, single-axis flip and rotation/scale have pixel tests on SDL_RENDERER and EasyGL.

Claim that Vulkan and other GPU families are not independently verified: VULKAN, SOFTWARE, OPENGL4 (parity corpus), DIRECTX11/12 (parity inventory) and FREEDIRECT now register SpriteFont pixel tests; other families still rely on shared code.
Claim that combined-axis flip is not representable on any renderer: it is representable and tested in the shared layer.

SDL_RENDERER bridges XNA's origin (maps to the destination position) and SDL_RenderTextureRotated's in-rectangle pivot by offsetting the destination by the scaled origin; an earlier build misplaced the pivot.

SDL_RENDERER applies a non-identity Begin transform through SDL_RenderTextureAffine (flips as corner permutations) and keeps the cheaper rotated call for the identity case; an earlier build ignored the transform.

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: Deferred defers the sort and the renderer calls, not a single GPU batch: the shared class coalesces sort decisions only.

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: pushSprite sends Immediate sprites straight to flushSingle and queues all others.

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: flushBatch optionally sorts and then calls the renderer once per sprite: about a thousand sprites give about a thousand ISpriteBatchRenderer::Draw calls.

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: Immediate is the only mode whose submissions keep their exact position relative to state changes at the shared seam, but EasyGL and Vulkan still batch below it, so texture contents rewritten between Draws are rasterised with final contents (a recorded divergence from XNA).

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: Claim that the batch coalesces sort decisions but never GPU draw calls: GPU families accumulate quads and flush per texture run (EasyGL/OpenGL4 2,048 sprites, D3D11 65,536 vertices, Vulkan FlushTexture), while SDL_RENDERER and DOM renderers issue one call per sprite.

concepts.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
concepts.text: pushSprite rejects a disposed texture with ObjectDisposedException as CNA-specific hardening against a null renderer dereference.
The resolved DepthStencilState (None for nullptr) is applied at the flush boundary and never inherited from a preceding 3D draw.
concepts.note: Applied at End for deferred modes, not at Begin.

concepts.text: End does not restore the earlier BlendState (same rule as the Begin blend-state section).
An earlier implementation accepted depthStencilState without applying it, so sprites inherited prior 3D state; applying the resolved state aligned the null case with FNA.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the state is resolved and applied; layerDepth tests run on SOFTWARE/GL/D3D11/12 builds.

concepts.text: MeasureString and DrawString are independent implementations of the same walk in two files; they agree glyph by glyph and differ only in the trailing-overhang width rule.

concepts.text: Claim that the first glyph adds abs(left bearing): at TARGET it adds max(left bearing, 0) and no Spacing (measured against XNA 4.0); FNA uses Math.Abs.
Later glyphs add Spacing plus the left bearing, unclamped.
After each glyph DrawString adds width plus right bearing.
The first-glyph clamp keeps a negative initial bearing from moving the string before position (glyph sits flush), while later negative bearings still tuck glyphs toward their predecessors.

concepts.text: MeasureString applies the same first-glyph rule, so measured and drawn placement agree.
The EasyGL fixture easygl_spritefont_multiglyph_spacing_test.cpp exercises the non-first branch with two 8 x 8 glyphs, kerning (0, 8, 0) and Spacing 4.
Drawing "AB" at (2, 2) places A at x in [2, 10) and B at [14, 22), leaving a 4-pixel background gap [10, 14) that proves Spacing was applied.
Distinct glyph colours rule out an index mix-up between glyphs, which a single-glyph test cannot detect.
Begin twice without End, and End without Begin, throw with the messages "Begin has been called before calling End." and "End was called, but Begin has not yet been called."

concepts.text: Claim that these guards throw std::runtime_error instead of XNA's InvalidOperationException: at TARGET they throw System::InvalidOperationException, as do Draw/DrawString before Begin.
Explanation that InvalidOperationException and std::runtime_error hierarchies meet only at std::exception, so a typed handler missed SpriteBatch misuse.
concepts.note: The mismatch it explains no longer exists: SpriteBatch throws System::InvalidOperationException (SpriteBatch.cpp Begin/End).

concepts.section: Where this leaves a porting engineer
concepts.text: SpriteBatch coverage is broad because every renderer must implement it, but evidence is not uniform: shared queue tests, renderer engagement, targeted pixel tests and XNA-oracle comparisons establish different claims.

issues.text: Only EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE override the sub-pixel SpriteBatch Draw; every other family truncates destinations to whole pixels.
Immediate mode on EasyGL and Vulkan rasterises all sprites of a batch against a texture's final contents (VULKAN-057).
EasyGL: full-back-buffer SpriteBatch draw before first 3D draw reportedly breaks the frame (Task 933); not reproduced by a later neutral scene.
SpriteFont pixel tests exist only for EasyGL, SDL_RENDERER, VULKAN, SOFTWARE, OPENGL4/D3D11/D3D12 parity and FREEDIRECT.

Rasterizer state ignored in Begin, integer quantisation in the shared layer, missing SpriteEffects operators, std::runtime_error guards and the D3D9 far-plane clip are absent at TARGET; CNA docs/spritefont-support.md is stale.
